Super Micro Computer has seen its share price swing sharply in recent years, which puts fresh attention on a simple question for you as an investor. Are you paying a sensible price for Super Micro Computer today given what its earnings are already delivering?

Over the past 5 years the stock has gained about 531.4%, so a lot of future profit expectations are already tied to where the valuation settles.

New AI focused server launches, partnerships and product architectures may support expectations for future profitability and influence how much investors are willing to pay for each dollar of earnings.

Your read on Super Micro Computer is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Super Micro Computer's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether Super Micro Computer's current share price can be justified by its earnings when judged against the Fair Ratio benchmark.

To pressure test Super Micro Computer's AI server story against similar themes, it can help to line it up beside other 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Does Super Micro Computer Look Undervalued on Earnings?

The P/E ratio is a useful lens here because Super Micro Computer is already profitable, so the share price can be lined up directly against current earnings. The stock trades on a P/E of about 5.6x, which is far below the broader Tech sector average of 16.2x and also well under the peer group on roughly 48.2x. That is a wide gap for a business positioned in AI infrastructure, where investors often pay a premium for every dollar of profit.

On this framework, the Fair Ratio, which blends Super Micro Computer's growth outlook, margin profile, size and risk into a single benchmark, points to a higher multiple than where the stock currently trades, so the shares screen as undervalued on earnings. Because the P/E looks compressed even after the recent recognition as an affordable AI data center stock with strong recent earnings momentum, the market is still pricing in more caution than the sector and peers. title: Super Micro Computer: Q1 Earnings Had Plenty to Cheer and Plenty to Worry About
detail:
Super Micro Computer: Q1 Earnings Had Plenty to Cheer and Plenty to Worry About
Sushree Mohanty
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 6:24 AM MST 6 min read
SMCI
Trade SMCI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Supermicro headquarters in San Jose, By JHVEPhoto

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) reported a strong start to fiscal 2027, giving investors plenty of reasons to cheer about. Revenue nearly quadrupled, earnings beat the company's own forecast, and management lifted the full-year sales target.

However, the headline growth hides a more complicated picture, which is probably why the market didn't react much to this enormous quarter. If anything, the stock has fallen 8.3% over the last five days and 7.6% so far this year.

Here are the red flags investors should consider before buying SMCI stock on the dip.

www.barchart.com
Red Flag No. 1: One Customer Makes Up Nearly Half of Revenue

Super Micro reported $19.9 billion in revenue in its fiscal first quarter, a 298% increase from last year and 79% higher than the previous quarter. This jump includes about $2.3 billion from projects delayed because customers and data centers weren't ready. Without that catch-up, revenue would have been around $17.6 billion. That's still a large number but gives investors a clearer picture of the company's regular pace this quarter.

The red flag here is who is buying these systems. A single, massive data center customer made up 44% of quarterly revenue, putting too many eggs in one basket. When so much depends on the unpredictable timing of huge infrastructure projects, that kind of reliance feels risky. At the end of the first quarter, just two customers made up 49% and 17% of accounts receivable. If one of these giants shifts its rollout, slows spending, or delays payment, it could impact revenue, inventory, and cash flow all at once.

Management said the concentration stems from the size of current AI infrastructure projects and expects it to lessen as enterprise and sovereign AI businesses grow. Some factors helped offset this. Notably, deferred revenue rose by $3.1 billion, mostly from customer payments made before delivery, and days sales outstanding dropped from 59 to 36. The company also reported no significant credit losses this quarter. These protections help for now, but the risk of relying on a few very large buyers remains.

title: Dell Sinks 12% in a Week on Texas Data Center Fears: “A Moratorium, a Ban”
detail:
Dell Sinks 12% in a Week on Texas Data Center Fears: “A Moratorium, a Ban”
Wiltone Asuncion

DELL

Dell Sinks 12% in a Week on Texas Data Center Fears: "A Moratorium, a Ban" ©@Lisa Fotios from Pexels via Canva, @Lisa Fotios from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Dell fell 12% in the week to Nov. 9 as AI hardware stocks, Nvidia and Super Micro among them, sold off after the Nov. 3 midterms.

As of Nov. 6, analysts hadn't cut Dell's earnings estimates.

At its five-year average forward P/E, the stock looks like a buy while AI orders hold up.

Dell's Nov. 24 report has to turn its AI backlog into cash, and a Texas moratorium is the main risk.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) fell 12% in the week to Nov. 9 with no news of its own. Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ), whose chips fill Dell's AI racks, fell 12% over the same stretch, including a 4% drop on Nov. 9 after its board opened an independent investigation into reports involving CEO Jensen Huang. Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ), Dell's AI server rival, gave sellers one more reason to go on election night.

Texas voters spooked the AI trade

In Texas, Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race after vowing "a moratorium, a ban, on all data center approvals" in an Oct. 22 video on X, as CNBC reported. Wells Fargo estimates Texas holds about 27% of planned US data center capacity.

Super Micro's sales nearly quadrupled from a year earlier to $19.9 billion in its September quarter, but its gross margin slid to 12.7% from 17.5% the quarter before. Selling more AI servers doesn't guarantee more profit on them.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Dell Technologies, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Dell Technologies' Analyst Ratings

The estimates haven't budged

For Dell, what matters is whether a moratorium cancels AI orders or moves them to other states. Dell's AI backlog hit a record $95 billion at the end of July. Nvidia's data center revenue jumped 117% to $89.0 billion in its July quarter, and it guided to $108.0 billion of total revenue for the October quarter. Nvidia reports on Nov. 17, a week before Dell, giving investors the first read on AI demand since the election.

As of Nov. 6, TIKR's consensus still had Dell earning $25.91 a share in the year ending January 2027 and $30.30 the year after.

Dell Technologies (DELL): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (years to January) (TIKR)

So the selloff came straight out of the multiple. Dell traded at about 12x forward earnings at its Nov. 6 close. That's right on its five-year average and under half its mid-August peak of 26x.

Dell Technologies (DELL): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)
The cash is the test on Nov. 24

Cash is the weak spot. First-half free cash flow was $4.1 billion, flat from a year earlier, while net income more than tripled to $7.6 billion. Financing Dell extends to customers buying its gear absorbed about $6.4 billion.
